explanation: [Er75h] p.2: for x₁, x₂, x₃ not on a line, Mrs. E. Szekeres observed there is a unique x₄ such that x₁,…,x₄ are not on a circle and the four circles determined by the triples have the same radius; take x₄ the orthocentre. The Lean statement adds the hypothesis that the triangle is not right-angled (for a right triangle the orthocentre is a vertex, so the literal claim fails), and requires the four points to be in general position with circleRadii having exactly one value. For non-right triangles the orthocentre H is off the circumcircle and off the side lines, and the circumradii of HAB, HBC, HCA equal that of ABC; uniqueness follows since four non-concyclic points with congruent triple-circumcircles form an orthocentric system. So the formal statement is a correct, documented repair of a literally false source claim — a sensible deviation from the source wording, disclosed in the docstring.
